title: Read the history
summary: The log lists commits. The short view helps you see their order and messages without opening each snapshot.
introduction: The log lists commits. The short view helps you see their order and messages without opening each snapshot. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: The log lists commits. The short view helps you see their order and messages without opening each snapshot.
The log shows the saved commits. HEAD names the current checked-out commit in this normal branch workflow.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Find the message for your first commit.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Commit IDs depend on repository content and metadata; your IDs will differ from another learner's.
For more detail later, use this [Git further reading](https://git-scm.com/docs/gittutorial).

seo.title: Git: Read the history
seo.description: Learn about read the history in Git. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
